src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: If the sun were suddenly replaced by a black hole of equal mass, what immediate change would occur to earth orbit?
o: Earth would spiral inward and be swallowed immediately
Earth's orbit would remain nearly the same initially
Earth would be sling shotted out of the solar system
Earth's orbit would decay slowly due to gravitational waves
x: A black hole of the Sun's mass would pull the Earth with the same gravity at the same distance, so the orbit would stay nearly the same (the Earth would only go dark and cold).

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Approximately how much time it takes for the Sunlight to reach Earth from the Sun?
x: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to cover the 149.6 million km to the Earth, so 8 minutes.

s: Unlike the fluid core of the Earth, the core of the moon is–
x: The question contrasts Earth's fluid (outer) core with the Moon's core, which books describe as solid; the Moon has in fact a small solid inner core with a fluid outer layer (NASA 2011). Off-topic (solar system), moved.

s:
Arrange the following planets in order of their nearness to the Sun

I. Mars
II. Mercury
III. Venus
IV. Earth
x: Order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars = II, III, IV, I. Off-topic (solar system), moved.

s:
Match the following.
List-I:
a. Titan
b. Ganymede
c. Phobos
d. Triton
List-II: i. Jupiter ii. Mars iii. Neptune iv. Saturn
The correct answer is:
x: Titan orbits Saturn, Ganymede Jupiter, Phobos Mars and Triton Neptune. Moved.

src: Assistant Director of Fisheries in AP Fisheries Service 2017
s: With which material the inter galactic space is filled up?
x: Intergalactic space is almost a perfect vacuum (a few atoms per cubic metre); air, oxygen, nitrogen, CO2 and ozone exist only in planetary atmospheres. No printed key; off-topic (universe), moved.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Which of the following continents witnessed total solar eclipse in August, 2017?
x: The total solar eclipse of 21 August 2017 crossed the USA coast to coast, i.e. North America. Moved to the solar-system row.

s: The bright outer layer of the Sun is known as :
x: The photosphere is the Sun's bright visible 'surface', emitting most of its light; ionosphere and mesosphere are layers of Earth's atmosphere and sunspots are dark patches on the photosphere.

s: In the universe, what are pulsars?
o: Radio waves emitted by a star
x: Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars that emit beams of radiation seen as regular pulses.

s: Highly dense stars are called –
x: Neutron stars – collapsed cores of massive stars – are the densest stars known; a supernova is an explosion and asteroids are not stars.

s:
Consider the following pairs : Objects in space Description
1. Cepheids : Giant clouds of dust and gas in space
2. Nebulae : Stars which brighten and dim periodically
3. Pulsars : Neutron stars that are formed when massive stars run out of fuel and collapse
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Only pair 3 is right: pulsars are neutron stars formed when massive stars collapse. Cepheids are stars that brighten and dim periodically, and nebulae are clouds of dust and gas – pairs 1 and 2 are swapped.

s: In January 2023, scientists at NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) announced the discovery of a planet named ____, slightly smaller in size than the earth, orbiting within the habitable zone of its star.
x: In January 2023 NASA's TESS mission announced TOI 700 e, slightly smaller than Earth, in the habitable zone of TOI 700 (TOI 700 d was found in 2020).

s: Which one of the following is a spacecraft?
x: Cassini (NASA–ESA, Saturn, RTG-powered) was a spacecraft; Apophis is an asteroid, Spitzer a space telescope and TecSAR an Israeli radar satellite.

s: The basic fuel for the thermo-nuclear reactions going on within the sun is
x: Hydrogen is the basic fuel of the Sun's thermonuclear (fusion) reactions, fusing into helium.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: What is the significance of graphic representation?
o: They make comparison of variables easy
Complete accuracy is not possible on a graph
Only a few characteristics can be depicted on a graph
x: Graphs and diagrams make comparison of variables easy at a glance; inaccuracy and the few traits shown are limitations, not the significance. Off-topic statistics, moved.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: If a ship is approaching the shore from the deep sea, which portion of the ship would be first seen by a person standing on the seashore?
x: Because the Earth's surface is curved, the top of the ship – the mast – is seen first and the hull last.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: The area represented by contours whose values decrease towards the centre (1300, 1280, 1260 from outer to inner) is a ____
x: Closed contours whose values fall towards the centre show a depression (hollow); rising values would show a hill. Off-topic (maps/contours), moved.

s:
Match the following:
List-I:
A. Longitude
B. Pole
C. Prime latitude
D. Axis
List-II:
I. Straight line
II. Circle
III. Semi circle
IV. Dot

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: A level surface is a surface ____ to the ____ of the earth
x: In surveying, a level surface is a curved surface parallel to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth (every point normal to the plumb line). Off-topic (geodesy/surveying), moved to Earth – shape and geoid.

s: A person stood alone in a desert on a dark night and wanted to reach his village which was situated 5 km east of the point where he was standing. He had no instruments to find the direction, but he located the polestar. The most convenient way now to reach his village is to walk in the:
o: direction keeping the polestar to his left
direction keeping the polestar to his right
x: The Pole Star marks north; facing east, north lies on your left, so he should walk keeping the Pole Star to his left.

s: The shape of the Earth's orbit is
x: Earth's orbit is an ellipse so close to a circle that it is only a slightly 'scaled' oval; 'elongated oval' exaggerates it and 'circular' ignores the small eccentricity (0.017).

src: Technical Assistant (Hydrology) & Laboratory Assistant in AP
s: The Indian City which experiences longest period of sunlight during summer is
x: Srinagar, the northernmost of these cities, has the longest summer day because day length in summer increases with latitude.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: Isogonic lines pass through points of ____
x: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination; isoclinic lines join points of equal dip.

s:
Match the following
List-I:
(A) Shale
(B) Limestone
(C) Coal
(D) Sandstone
List-II: (i) Quartzite (ii) Diamond (iii) Slate (iv) Marble
x: Shale → slate, limestone → marble, coal → diamond (the textbook pairing; strictly graphite), sandstone → quartzite. Moved to rocks.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Two statements are given labelled as
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
Select the correct option based on the given statements.
Assertion (A): Felsic rocks contain relatively high amounts of iron, magnesium, and calcium.
Reason (R): Olivine and Pyroxene are dark in colour.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
x: A is false: felsic rocks are rich in silica, feldspar and aluminium, while mafic rocks are rich in iron and magnesium. R is true: olivine and pyroxene are dark. Moved to Geography.

s: What is mountain building by folding and faulting due to horizontal (tangential) forces called?
x: Orogenic movements act through horizontal forces and build mountains such as the Himalayas.

s: Which forces mainly cause epeirogenic movements?
x: Epeirogenic movements are vertical and uplift or warp continents and plateaus.

s:
Consider the following statements about diastrophism:
1. Orogenic movements uplift or warp whole continents and plateaus.
2. Sudden movements such as earthquakes and volcanoes are treated separately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Uplift or warping of continents is epeirogenic, not orogenic; sudden movements are treated separately.

s:
Consider the following statements about the development of folds with increasing pressure:
1. A symmetrical fold comes before an asymmetrical fold.
2. A nappe forms before a recumbent fold.
3. A recumbent fold forms after an asymmetrical fold.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is symmetrical, asymmetrical, recumbent and finally nappe, so a nappe forms after (not before) a recumbent fold.

s: In plate-tectonic terms, what are the Eastern Ghats?
o: Old, highly eroded, discontinuous hills of the stable Gondwana shield
Block mountains of recently uplifted nappes
Young fold mountains formed by recent continental collision
Volcanic hills formed along a rift
x: The Eastern Ghats are old, highly eroded and discontinuous hills of the stable Gondwana shield, not young fold mountains.

s: What are an up-arched fold and a down-troughed fold respectively called?
x: An anticline is an up-arched fold, while a syncline is a down-troughed fold. Horst and graben are fault blocks, not folds.

s: Which one of the following is an old fold mountain range?
x: The Aravallis are old, worn-down fold mountains and are among the oldest mountain systems in India.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Alps – Young fold mountains of Europe
Appalachians – Old fold mountains of North America
Urals – Old fold mountains along the Europe–Asia divide
Rockies – Old fold mountains of North America
x: The Rockies are young fold mountains of North America; the Appalachians are the old ones.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Himalayas?
o: Their formation began about 70 million years ago and continues at present
They were formed from sediments of the Tethys Sea
Their uplift is associated with the Eocene, Miocene and Pliocene epochs
The Siwaliks are the oldest Himalayan range
x: The Siwaliks are the youngest Himalayan range, not the oldest.

s: With rising pressure, which fold forms next after an asymmetrical fold?
x: The sequence is symmetrical, asymmetrical, overfold, recumbent and nappe.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an old fold mountain?
x: The Rockies are young (Tertiary/Alpine) fold mountains; the Aravallis, Appalachians and Urals are old, worn-down folds.

s: Which is the youngest Himalayan range, with simple Jura-type folds?
x: The Siwaliks are the youngest Himalayan range and show simple Jura-type folds.

s: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is bounded by which of the following fault systems?
o: Two thrust faults on both sides
A normal fault in the north and the Himalayan Frontal Fault in the south
The Himalayan Frontal Fault in the north and a normal fault in the south
Two strike-slip faults in the north and south
x: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is bounded by the Himalayan Frontal Fault to the north and a normal fault to the south.

s: Which of the following is an example of a block mountain in India?
x: The Satpura is a block mountain, flanked by the rift valleys of the Narmada and Tapi.

s: The Himalayan MCT, MBT and HFF are examples of which one of the following?
x: The Himalayan Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault are examples of thrust faults.

s: What is a low-angle reverse fault called?
x: A thrust fault is a low-angle reverse fault; in a normal fault the hanging wall moves down and a strike-slip fault moves horizontally.

s: Which lake lies at the southern end of the East African Rift?
x: The East African Rift holds a series of mostly freshwater lakes with Lake Malawi at its southern end; Lake Victoria lies between the two branches and is not a rift lake.

s: In the Vosges–Rhine example, what is the Rhine Valley?
x: The Rhine Valley is a graben (sunken block); the Vosges are horsts, i.e. block mountains.

s: The Satpura is a block mountain lying between the rift valleys of which rivers?
x: The Satpura is a block mountain between the rift valleys of the Narmada and Tapi.

s: What are horsts also known as?
x: A horst is an uplifted block between faults, so it forms a block mountain; a sunken block (graben) forms a rift valley.

s: Which of the following lakes is NOT a rift lake of the East African Rift?
x: Lake Victoria lies in a shallow basin between the rift arms, so it is not a rift lake; Lake Malawi lies at the rift's southern end.

s: Which force produces a normal fault?
x: A normal fault forms under tension, with the hanging wall moving down; reverse and thrust faults form under compression.

s: In a reverse fault, which force acts and how does the hanging wall move?
x: A reverse fault forms under compression and its hanging wall moves up; a normal fault forms under tension.

s:
Following are the intrusive landforms of volcanic activity and their characteristic features:

I. Batholiths: Huge mass of igneous rocks, usually granite at the deeper layers of the crust.

II. Phacoliths: Large igneous mounds with a dome-shaped upper surface.

III. Dykes: Wall-like structures developed by solidifying almost perpendicular to the ground.

IV. Sills: The near horizontal bodies of intrusive igneous rocks.
Which of the above are correctly matched?
x: A large dome-shaped mound is a laccolith; a phacolith is a wavy, lens-shaped mass at the base of synclines or top of anticlines, so II is wrong. Moved.

s: Barren island is located in-
x: Barren Island, India's only active volcano, lies in the Andaman Sea, Bay of Bengal, ~135 km NE of Port Blair. Moved.

s:
With reference to 'Indonesia', which of the following statements is / are correct?
(1) It comprises of over 15,000 islands.
(2) It has over 150 active volcanoes.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Code:
x: Indonesia has about 17,000 islands but roughly 127–130 active volcanoes, fewer than 150, so only statement 1 is correct. Moved.

s: The most active Volcano is –
x: Kilauea (Hawaii) is commonly cited as the world's most active volcano; Vesuvius and Fuji are dormant-to-active, Cotopaxi less frequent. Moved.

s: Which gas is present in the greatest proportion among the principal gases released by volcanoes?
x: Volcanic gases consist mostly of water vapour, followed by carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and hydrogen sulphide.

s: Composite or stratovolcanoes constitute approximately what share of the Earth's volcanoes?
x: Composite volcanoes, with viscous lava, steep cones and explosive eruptions, make up approximately 60% of Earth's volcanoes.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mauna Loa — caldera formed by explosive collapse
Mount Aso — one of the world's largest calderas
Etna — complex volcano with several overlapping vents only
Dukono — shield volcano with gentle basaltic slopes
x: Mount Aso is one of the world's largest calderas. Mauna Loa is a shield volcano, while Dukono is listed as a complex volcano.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a complex or compound volcano?
x: Taal in the Philippines is a complex or compound volcano. Dukono is in Indonesia, while Mount Aso is a caldera in Japan.

s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Strombolian and Vulcanian eruptions?
o: Vulcanian eruptions consist only of gentle lava flows.
Strombolian eruptions are frequent and mild, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.
Strombolian eruptions are always more explosive than Vulcanian eruptions.
Both terms refer exclusively to dormant volcanoes.
x: Strombolian eruptions involve frequent, mild bursts of bombs and ash, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.

s: In which country is Mount Aso, among the world's largest calderas, located?
x: Mount Aso in Japan is a caldera, among the world's largest.

s: Which one of the following is an extrusive volcanic landform?
x: Lava plateaus, cinder and composite cones, craters, calderas and lava flows are extrusive volcanic landforms. Batholiths, lopoliths and phacoliths are intrusive forms.

s: What is a vertical wall of igneous rock cutting across the rock beds called?
x: A dyke is a vertical wall cutting across beds; a sill is a horizontal sheet parallel to the beds. Dykes fed the Deccan Traps.

s: What is a large, often dome-shaped mass of granite occurring at great depth and exposed after denudation called?
x: A batholith is a huge mass of granite emplaced at depth. It may become exposed after denudation removes the overlying rocks.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lopolith — wavy mass in a folded structure
Phacolith — wavy mass at the base of a syncline or top of an anticline
Laccolith — vertical wall cutting across rock beds
x: A phacolith is a wavy intrusive mass occurring at the base of a syncline or the top of an anticline. A lopolith is saucer-shaped, a laccolith is dome-shaped with a flat base, and a dyke is a vertical wall.

s: What is a dome-shaped intrusive body with a flat base, fed by a pipe from below, called?
x: Domes with a flat base are laccoliths; a phacolith is a wavy mass, so calling phacoliths large domed mounds is wrong.

s: With which hotspot are the Deccan Traps, the fissure basalts of the end-Cretaceous, linked?
x: The Deccan Traps formed about 65 million years ago from the Reunion hotspot.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Barren Island – Only active volcano of India
x: Narcondam is dormant, not extinct; Dhinodhar in Kutch is the extinct one.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Mount Etna is correct?
o: It is Europe's largest and most active volcano, rises to about 3,300 m and became a UNESCO site in 2013.
It is Africa's highest peak and has been dormant since 1707.
It is the world's highest active volcano at 6,893 m.
It is an extinct volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79.
x: Etna is Europe's largest and most active volcano, is approximately 3,300 m high and has been a UNESCO site since 2013.

s: White Island (Whakaari), a volcano that erupted in December 2019, is located in which country?
x: White Island (Whakaari) is in New Zealand and erupted in December 2019. Indonesia has Krakatoa and Dukono, Japan has Fujiyama and Mount Aso, and the Philippines has Taal and Mayon.

s: Which volcano is associated with the burial of Pompeii in AD 79?
x: Mount Vesuvius is an active volcano in Italy and buried Pompeii in AD 79.

s: Which is the world's highest active volcano?
x: Ojos del Salado in Chile (6,893 m) is the world's highest active volcano; Mauna Loa is the largest.

s:
Consider the following statements about Fujiyama:
1. It is a dormant volcano.
2. Its last eruption was in 1707.
3. It is Europe's largest and most active volcano.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Fujiyama in Japan is dormant and last erupted in 1707; Europe's largest and most active volcano is Etna.

s: What is the status of Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak?
x: Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) in Tanzania is dormant, unlike the active Italian volcanoes.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mauna Loa – Lighthouse of the Mediterranean
Mount St. Helens – Fujiyama of America
x: Mount St. Helens is the 'Fujiyama of America'; Stromboli is the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean and Mauna Loa means 'Long Mountain'.

s: In which country is the Mayon volcano, a symmetrical composite cone, located?
x: Mayon in the Philippines is a symmetrical composite cone on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

s: In which year did the Krakatoa volcano of Indonesia erupt, causing great tsunamis?
x: Krakatoa, between Java and Sumatra, erupted in 1883 and caused tsunamis.

s: The scientist who conducted comprehensive research on the earthquakes that occurred in Himalayan mountains prior to 1890s was
x: R.D. Oldham of the Geological Survey of India studied the Himalayan/Assam earthquakes (report on the great 1897 Assam earthquake) and later identified the Earth's core from seismic waves. Moved to Earthquakes.

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s:
Which of the following Statements is most appropriate?

I. Earthquakes do not kill people

II. It is badly designed buildings that kill people
o: Statement I is True and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Both Statements are true and Statement II is the reason behind Statement I
x: Both are true and II explains I: earthquakes themselves rarely kill; most deaths come from the collapse of badly designed, non-engineered buildings – hence earthquake-resistant codes.

src: APPSC Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Serv
s: Which of the following is likely to kill more people?
x: Earthquakes kill mainly through the collapse of badly designed buildings; hazards in empty deserts, the deep sea or deep forests kill few. Off-topic (earthquake risk), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
s: Out of the following, which major disaster struck India in the year 2001?
x: The Bhuj (Gujarat) earthquake struck on 26 January 2001; Kedarnath was 2013, Kumbakonam fire 2004 and the tsunami December 2004. Moved to row 10.

src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-I Screening Test 2017
s: The ground shaking during an earthquake would be higher in
o: Shaking does not vary with soil type
x: Soft, loose soils amplify seismic waves and shake more (and may liquefy), while hard rock shakes least.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: The movement of earthy materials from higher region to lower region due to gravitational pull is called
x: The downslope movement of earth material under gravity is mass movement; its sudden form is a landslide. Off-topic (mass wasting), moved.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: What is measured in cubic/sec?
x: Cubic metres (or feet) per second – cumecs/cusecs – measure discharge, the rate of water flow in a river or canal. Off-topic (river discharge), moved.

s: Drumlins are found in?
x: Drumlins are inverted-boat-shaped mounds of glacial till, so they are found in glaciated areas such as Himalayan glaciers, not oceans, deserts or deltas.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Over which of the following regions is the major ozone hole of the Earth?
x: The ozone hole forms over Antarctica every southern spring, when polar stratospheric clouds help chlorine destroy ozone; the Arctic loss is much smaller. Moved to the atmosphere row.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The largest ozone hole is observed over
x: The largest (seasonal) ozone hole lies over Antarctica, not over Africa, Australia or India. Moved to the atmosphere row.

s: In absorption of insolation, the most significant part is played by
x: Of the options, carbon dioxide (with water vapour, not offered) absorbs the most insolation over a broad band; ozone absorbs only a small share (UV), and oxygen and haze little. Moved to insolation and heat budget.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statement-I: The atmosphere is heated more by incoming solar radiation than by terrestrial radiation.
2. Statement II: Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are good absorbers of longwave radiation. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
x: Statement I is wrong: the atmosphere is mostly transparent to incoming short-wave radiation and is heated mainly by terrestrial (long-wave) radiation. Statement II is right: CO2 and other GHGs absorb long-wave radiation. Moved to heat budget.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: In which of the following places, boiling point of water would be higher compared to others?
x: Water boils at a higher temperature where air pressure is higher, that is, at the lowest altitude. Visakhapatnam is a sea-level port, Kolleru is a low inland delta lake, and Tirumala and Nanda Devi are high up. The intended answer is the sea-level city, Visakhapatnam (no official key found; Kolleru is also near sea level).

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: In normal atmosphere, at which temperature, evaporation of water takes place?
x: Evaporation goes on at all temperatures (from the surface of a liquid); 100°C is the boiling point. Belongs to row 17 (evaporation), moved.

src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of

x: Cumulonimbus clouds, tall and dense, bring thunderstorms and heavy rain.

Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S

0.5°C warmer than average for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods

s: Who described the Southern Oscillation in 1920?

s: What does the Southern Oscillation represent in ENSO?

s: How often does El Nino recur on average?

s: What does a negative Southern Oscillation Index (Tahiti minus Darwin) indicate?
